newsitem.title: UK: Shell Nigeria now running 160,000 bpd below normal.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria now running 160,000 bpd below normal.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell's Nigerian crude oil output recovered a little on Monday but was still running 160,000 barrels a day (bpd) below normal capacity, a company official in Lagos said.
Shell Nigeria was pumping at 790,000 bpd on Monday compared to normal output of around 950,000 bpd, the official familiar with export schedules said.

Shell production last week slipped to 210,000 bpd below normal after a political dispute saw local villagers occupy Shell pumping stations in both the western and eastern divisions of the company's Niger Delta operations.
Shell Nigeria now running 160,000 bpd below =2
Production at Shell's Bonny operations east of the Niger had recovered to 410,000 bpd on Monday, 40,000 bpd below normal, after it brought back onstream one of five flow stations in Nembe Creek.
"Production is stepping back up," the official said. "We expect to be back to normal (Bonny output) by the end of the week.
But output of Forcados west of the Niger on Monday was running at 380,000 bpd, the Shell official said.
The Shell official said latest information was that only two of 12 flow stations put out of action in total by the communal disturbances across the Niger delta were back to work.
"Two are up, but 10 are still down," he said.
The occupation of flow stations near Warri, the centre of Shell's Forcados operations, ended last Thursday when protesters freed the last batch of 53 Shell workers being held hostage.
Operations resumed on Friday at one Nembe Creek flow station, part of the Bonny system, after agreement with the local community.
Shell so far has managed to avoid cancelling export shipments by taking crude from storage, which was brimful before the disturbances began 10 days ago.

An official with Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) said at the weekend that four companies scheduled to lift Forcados in early April had been informed that their cargoes would be delayed by about three days.
Shell declared force majeure last week warning lifters of the possibility of 2-3 day delays.
The NNPC official said that any decision on cancellations would be left until Tuesday after the long Easter weekend.
